message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Red blood cells** (which lack mitochondria) | 0 |
| **Neurons** (high energy demand) | 1 000–10 000 per cell |
| **Muscle cells** (especially cardiac or skeletal) | 5 000–20 000 per cell |
| **Liver hepatocytes** | 1 000–5 000 per cell |
| **Epithelial cells** (e.g., intestinal) | 200–1 000 per cell |
| **Stem cells** (low energy demand) | 100–500 per cell |

So, in a typical somatic cell you can expect anywhere from a few hundred to several thousand mitochondria. The exact number depends on the cell’s metabolic needs, developmental stage, and environmental conditions.
